source_refs.note: Book p. 260-261: heading printed 14.1.2 (no 14.1.1); three perpendicular axes, drawing convention, right-hand rule, point P(a, b, c); 3 figures. Book error: 'curled images toward'. Teaching notes, Key points, Common mistakes are ours.

items.title: 14.1.1 Rectangular Coordinate System in Space (Roman Urdu)

blocks.title: Numbering note
blocks.text: Kitab is heading ko 14.1.2 chhaapti hai (Book# 14.1.2). Kitab mein 14.1.1 naam ki koi heading hai hi nahin, is liye portal 14.1 ke sub-headings ko tarteeb se 14.1.1 se 14.1.8 tak number karta hai. Yahan 14.1.1 wahi hai jo kitab mein 14.1.2 hai.

Bachon, plane (kaghaz ki satah) mein kisi point ko batane ke liye do numbers kaafi the: \((x, y)\). Lekin agar main poochoon ke kamre mein lattoo (bulb) kahan laga hai, to sirf farsh par jagah batana kaafi nahin, unchai bhi batani paregi. Isi liye space mein teesra axis, z-axis, aata hai. Is subtopic mein hum dekhenge ke yeh teen axes kaise banaye aur kaghaz par kaise draw kiye jaate hain, aur un ki simt yaad rakhne ka right hand rule kya hai.

Space mein rectangular coordinate system teen aise axes se banta hai jo aapas mein mutually orthogonal (har ek doosre do par perpendicular, yani 90 degree par) hon, aur jin ka common point of intersection (milne ka nuqta) origin ho. Figure banate waqt hum yeh tareeqa (convention) apnaate hain: positive x-axis parhne wale ki taraf (aap ki taraf, kaghaz se baahar), positive y-axis daayen taraf aur positive z-axis upar ki taraf.

blocks.alt: Three perpendicular axes meeting at one point: the z-axis points up, the y-axis points to the right and the x-axis slants down to the left, toward the reader. The negative halves x′, y′ and z′ are dashed.
blocks.caption: Rectangular coordinate system in space: x toward the reader, y to the right, z upwards (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Apne class room ke kisi kone ko dekhiye. Farsh ke saath chalne wale do kinare x-axis aur y-axis hain, aur jahan do deewarein milti hain woh khara kinara z-axis hai; kona khud origin \(O\) hai. Har axis ka ek positive hissa hai (seedhi line) aur ek negative hissa (dashed line \(x'\), \(y'\), \(z'\)).
Kyun: x-axis tircha (slant) kyun banate hain? Kaghaz flat hai, is liye hum asal mein kaghaz se baahar aati line nahin bana sakte. Tirchi line aankh ko gehrai (depth) ka ehsaas deti hai, bilkul jaise drawing mein dabba (box) banate waqt peeche wale kinare tirche banaate hain.

Yeh axes right-hand rule (seedhe haath ka qaida) ke mutabiq label kiye jaate hain. Seedhe haath ki ungliyan positive x-axis ki simt mein rakhiye, phir unhein positive y-axis ki taraf mor (curl) dijiye; is waqt angootha (thumb) positive z-axis ki simt batayega.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab yahan "curled images toward the positive y-axis" likhti hai. Lafz "images" chhapai ki ghalti hai; sahi matlab: ungliyan positive x-axis ki simt se positive y-axis ki taraf mori jaati hain, aur angootha positive z-axis dikhata hai.

blocks.alt: Flat drawing of a right hand making a fist, the four fingers curled and the thumb pointing straight up; a black arrow runs up along the thumb. Pink panel with the label Right hand rule at the bottom.
blocks.caption: Right hand rule: fingers curl from +x toward +y, the thumb gives +z (original drawing after the textbook's picture)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Abhi kar ke dekhiye: seedha haath seedha rakhiye, ungliyan x-axis ki taraf, phir unhein y-axis ki taraf moriye aur dekhiye angootha kidhar hai. Wahi +z hai. Jo system is qaide ko maane use right-handed system kehte hain.
Kyun ahem hai: agar aap x aur y axes ki jagah badal dein to angootha neeche ki taraf jaayega; yeh left-handed system ban jaata hai. Hum hamesha right-handed axes istemaal karte hain, kyunke 14.3 mein cross product ki simt isi qaide par chalti hai. Agar yahan simt ghalat ho gayi to aage ke jawabon ka sign ulat jaayega.

blocks.title: Dhyan dein
blocks.text: Right hand rule hamesha seedhe (right) haath se lagaiye. Exam hall mein bohat se students baayen haath se pen pakre hote hain aur ghalti se wohi haath ghuma dete hain; is se jawab ulta aata hai.

Space mein kisi point \(P\) ke teen coordinates hote hain: ek x-axis ke saath, doosra y-axis ke saath aur teesra z-axis ke saath. Agar x-axis, y-axis aur z-axis ke saath faasle tarteeb se \(a\), \(b\) aur \(c\) hon, to point \(P\) ko real numbers ki ek unique triple (teen numbers ka tarteeb wala majmooa) se \(P(a, b, c)\) likhte hain (figure dekhiye). Unique ka matlab: har point ki sirf ek hi triple hoti hai, aur har triple sirf ek hi point batati hai.

blocks.alt: Axes x, y and z from O. A point P(a, b, c) is shown with dashed lines: a vertical dashed line of length c drops from P to the xy-plane, and from its foot two dashed lines run parallel to the axes, one of length a (parallel to the x-axis) and one of length b (parallel to the y-axis).
blocks.caption: The point P(a, b, c): distances a, b, c along the x-, y- and z-axes (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
\(P(2, 3, 4)\) kaise plot karein: \(O\) se shuru kijiye, x-axis ke saath 2 unit chaliye, phir y-axis ke parallel 3 unit, phir z-axis ke parallel 4 unit upar. Numbers ki tarteeb hamesha pehle \(x\), phir \(y\), phir \(z\).
Khaas points: \((a, 0, 0)\) x-axis par hai, \((0, b, 0)\) y-axis par aur \((0, 0, c)\) z-axis par. Jis point mein \(z = 0\) ho, jaise \((2, 3, 0)\), woh xy-plane (farsh) mein hai; \(x = 0\) se yz-plane aur \(y = 0\) se xz-plane milta hai. Yeh teen coordinate planes space ko aath hisson mein baant dete hain jinhein octants kehte hain.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
Yeh points kahan hain? (1) \((0, 0, 5)\) (2) \((3, 0, 0)\) (3) \((2, 4, 0)\) (4) \((0, -1, 6)\).
Jawab: (1) z-axis par, origin se 5 unit upar; (2) x-axis par, aap ki taraf 3 unit; (3) xy-plane (farsh) mein; (4) yz-plane mein, kyunke \(x = 0\) hai.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text: (Hamari practice.) Kamre ka ek kona origin maan lijiye aur faasle metres mein. Ek bulb farsh ke kone se x-taraf 2 m, y-taraf 3 m aur 2.5 m ki unchai par laga hai. Us ke coordinates \((2, 3, 2.5)\) hain. Agar bulb ko seedha neeche farsh par laaya jaaye to sirf unchai sifar hogi: \((2, 3, 0)\). Is se pata chalta hai ke z-coordinate sirf unchai batata hai, aur pehle do coordinates farsh par jagah.

Ek aakhri baat: 3D figure kaghaz par hamesha thora sa dhoka deta hai, kyunke tirchi x-axis par 1 unit chhota nazar aata hai. Is liye figure se lambai naap kar jawab kabhi mat nikaaliye; figure sirf samajhne ke liye hai, hisaab hamesha coordinates aur formulas se kijiye.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
Teen aapas mein perpendicular axes origin \(O\) par milte hain.
Drawing ka tareeqa: +x aap ki taraf, +y daayen, +z upar.
Right-hand rule: ungliyan +x se +y ki taraf moriye, angootha +z.
Space ke har point ki ek unique triple \((x, y, z)\) hai; \(O = (0, 0, 0)\).

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
Coordinates ki tarteeb badal dena: \((2, 3, 4)\) aur \((3, 2, 4)\) alag points hain.
Plane graph ki tarah x-axis daayen taraf bana dena: space mein +x aap ki taraf aata hai aur +y daayen.
Rule ke liye baayan haath istemaal karna: angootha ulti simt dikhayega.
